prize_parts.citation: for empirical analysis of how trade exposure and technological change reshape local labour markets, employment and wages

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1. I still propose B038 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn, and I have not moved on the substance. The contribution is a body of evidence on how import competition and technology change employment, earnings and the geography of adjustment. It uses transparent local-labour-market variation and has been replicated, criticised and extended for over a decade. What it established is that adjustment costs to trade shocks were large, persistent and concentrated, which the earlier consensus had not expected. That finding changed research in labour, trade and political economy, and it changed how adjustment costs enter policy debate. The chair's round-1 question asks whether a citation limited to trade and technology exposure and local adjustment can settle the third name. I think it can, and it settles it for Dorn. Dorn is a full co-author of the central China-shock papers and of the Autor-Dorn work on polarisation and service jobs. Katz's contribution to wage structure and the education-technology race is real, but it supports a differently framed prize. I would not use Katz to patch this one. I judge B038 on the common criteria of a specific discovery, credible design, durability and clean credit. I do not rank it by how many colleagues listed it. The colleagues' exchange sharpened the citation but did not change my ranking.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still bundling and coherence. The task and polarisation framework has a lineage (Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu) outside the credited names, and a trade-shock trio only partly covers it. The citation must therefore be written narrowly around exposure and local adjustment. The size and long-run persistence of the China-shock effects are debated, and shift-share instruments have drawn serious methodological criticism. Adjacent recent prizes on labour-market topics, technology and institutions may reduce the Committee's appetite for this ground. The attribution is defensible rather than unique, because Katz and others have legitimate claims to neighbouring strands. I also have a methodological affinity with natural-experiment and register-based work, so I may be inclined to favour B038 and B002 on grounds of design. I name that risk openly, and it is why I am wary of letting it decide the comparison with the theory-driven candidates.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B038 first, with Autor, Dorn and Hanson. Her citation names both an empirical and a conceptual element, covering trade exposure, labour demand and wage inequality. She accepts that the task lineage extends beyond the trio and that magnitudes are contested.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on Dorn over Katz. My difference with her is citation scope. Her wording credits an explanatory framework to these three, and I think that overreaches given the task-framework lineage she concedes. I would keep the citation to the empirical analysis of trade and technology exposure and local adjustment. Autor's link to the task view then stays visible without the citation claiming it. Her point that the shift-share critique has refined practice and not overturned the core finding matches my reading. Neither of us has independently re-checked that, so I treat it as a judgement and not a verified fact.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B038 seventh. He doubts that shift-share identification withstands current scrutiny, notes that the task framework owes much to uncredited scholars, and sees overlap with recent technology and institutions prizes. He would be more comfortable if the achievement were defined as the China-shock evidence alone.
responses.response: His proposal to define the achievement narrowly is close to my own citation, so part of his objection is met. I accept that the identification criticism is a real discount on magnitudes. I do not think it removes the qualitative finding. That finding comes from several outcomes, from pre-trend checks and from follow-up work with other exposure measures. These are the kinds of checks I would want, and I cannot independently confirm them here. On prior-prize overlap, I think the 2024 prize addressed long-run institutional determinants of prosperity. That is a different object from measured adjustment to trade and technology shocks, even though the topics are neighbours. I would give the overlap less weight than the substance, and I recognise that he weighs it more heavily.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B013 first. He accepts that the empirical support for Protection for Sale is mixed but argues the framework organised later empirical work. He has also moved toward Autor, Hanson and Dorn as the more defensible B038 grouping, and he places Katz's contribution on B002 or a separate wage-structure claim.
responses.response: I appreciate that he shares the attribution reasoning on B038. It is one reason I treat the Dorn question as largely settled. I opened with B013 first myself and still regard Grossman-Helpman as the cleaner pair on attribution and maturity. I weigh the mixed record of the specific predictions more heavily than he does, because I give priority to work whose identifying content can be examined against data. B013 therefore stays a close alternative and not my lead. On the chair's question about Helpman, I would credit him with Grossman for the political-economy and growth strands. The firm-heterogeneity framing is a rival configuration with a different originator. On Katz, I do not propose him on B002 either. His role there is tied to the Moving to Opportunity experiment and overlaps B038, which is a further reason not to settle either ballot by moving him.

responses.point: Dreber ranks B002 first with Chetty, Hendren and Friedman. She treats timing and restricted-data replication as the main risks and separates the descriptive mobility measurement from the causal movers and exposure-effects designs. She would weight the causal designs more heavily when judging durability.
responses.response: Her separation of measurement from causal design is the one I find most useful, and I share her view that the causal strand carries both the value and the uncertainty. It is why B002 is my second alternative and not my lead. The central results are about a decade old, and independent checks depend on restricted data. Her own metascience emphasis points to the same discount, and I would count it against maturity. If B002 advanced, I would support Chetty, Hendren and Friedman, with the citation naming measurement and place effects. I would not want the Committee to let the descriptive atlas carry a prize whose durability depends on the causal estimates. Our disagreement is about timing this year and not about quality.

uncertainties: How persistent and how large the China-shock effects are in the long run, and whether the shift-share criticism will further reduce confidence in the magnitudes.
Whether the Committee will accept a citation limited to exposure and local adjustment, or whether the unclaimed task-framework lineage will make a B038 prize look incomplete.
Whether proximity to recent prizes on labour-market topics, technology and institutions lowers the Committee's appetite for B038, and on what common standard.
Whether B002 matures enough in the Committee's view, and how much restricted data should discount confidence in the causal place-effect estimates.
Whether my identification-based criteria undervalue durable conceptual contributions such as B013 or B001.
My assessments rely on the supplied evidence and general knowledge, without independent verification of the literature.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific connection is apparent from the supplied profile. My listed co-authors (Holmlund, Edin, Åslund, Öckert, Johansson, Nybom, Oosterbeek, van Ours) are not credited names on B038, B013 or B002. I disclose that my class-size paper with Öckert and Oosterbeek (2013) is cited in the 2021 Scientific Background for the Card, Angrist and Imbens prize. This is not a connection to any 2026 candidate, but it shows that my work belongs to the same research tradition as B038 and B002. I chaired the Committee for the 2021 and 2020 announcements and gave the 2021 presentation speech. Those texts reflect Academy drafting and do not show a preference for any 2026 candidate. I have not adjudicated these ties.
